definition: Ventriculomegaly is an enlargement of the brain’s ventricles, the spaces that contain cerebrospinal fluid. In this packet, it is described as a feature of idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus and can also occur without that disorder’s symptoms.

reasons: The definition states that ventricles are “the spaces that contain cerebrospinal fluid,” but this anatomical description is not provided in the supplied packet text.

While the packet supports that ventriculomegaly is marked in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus and that there is a comparison group with ventriculomegaly but no iNPH symptoms, the definition’s first sentence includes an additional substantive claim not supported by the packet.
The phrase “the brain’s ventricles” / “the spaces that contain cerebrospinal fluid” is not supported by the packet; the packet only says ventriculomegaly is associated with ventricular enlargement.

The requested field “cognition” is not well supported for this term; the packet uses ventriculomegaly in an iNPH research context, but the term itself is a structural finding rather than a cognition concept.
